primary_reviews.support: Jer.8.4-Jer.8.17: Rhetorical questions about falling and turning introduce perpetual backsliding, false speech, and migratory birds that know their seasons. The claim to wisdom and Torah is answered by the lying pen, captured sages, universal greed, superficial healing, and a repeated shameless-fall verdict. Failed fruit harvest moves into communal flight speech, approaching cavalry, and the divine release of uncharmable serpents.

issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, Jer.23.16-Jer.23.22, Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32, Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40. Controlling evidence: The prophets heading and Jeremiah's broken-heart reaction introduce adulterous land, polluted temple figures, Samaria-Jerusalem comparison, and wormwood punishment. Scoped seam: Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15. The audience is forbidden to heed heart-visions promising peace; storm imagery and the divine-council test expose prophets who were neither sent nor corrective. Scoped seam: Jer.23.16-Jer.23.22. Near-and-far questions open an omnipresence claim, followed by lying-dream reports, straw-grain contrast, fire-and-hammer word imagery, and three behold-I-am-against verdicts. Scoped seam: Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32. An anticipated question about the divine burden is overturned through repeated burden-language and ends in lasting reproach and shame. Scoped seam: Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: A break after 23:12 would detach the named prophetic corruption from its comparative proof and sentence. Rejected-route scope: Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15. Extending to 23:32 would merge the council criterion with a new sequence of omnipresence, dream, and word-fire tests. Rejected-route scope: Jer.23.16-Jer.23.22. Dividing at 23:28 would separate the word-quality test from the repeated judgments against those who fail it. Rejected-route scope: Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32. Joining the fig vision at 24:1 would cross from lexical disputation to a dated symbolic vision. Rejected-route scope: Jer.23.33-Jer.23.40.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the yoke sign, royal warning, and priest-people warning surface as audience-specific children, or remain one sign-act dossier despite regnal and name pressure?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.27.1-11, Jer.27.12-15, and Jer.27.16-22 with yoke-dossier hydration | retain Jer.27.1-22 as the only surfaced sign, envoy, king, and temple-vessel warning unit
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11, Jer.27.12-Jer.27.15, Jer.27.16-Jer.27.22. Controlling evidence: A received regnal superscription introduces yoke-making and delivery through foreign envoys; Jeremiah's creation-sovereignty speech offers submission-life or resistance-judgment outcomes. Scoped seam: Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11. Jeremiah directly applies the yoke sign to the king, repeating submit-and-live counsel and exposing unsent prophets promising non-service. Scoped seam: Jer.27.12-Jer.27.15. A new priest-and-people address rejects quick vessel-return prophecies, challenges claimants to intercede, and promises that remaining vessels stay in Babylon until a later visitation. Scoped seam: Jer.27.16-Jer.27.22.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Separating 27:1 from 27:2 or cutting before 27:4 would detach date and performance from the envoy message, while the regnal-name tension must not be harmonized. Rejected-route scope: Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11. Merging the priests-and-people address at 27:16 would conceal the clear royal-to-public audience transition. Rejected-route scope: Jer.27.12-Jer.27.15. Folding this into the royal exhortation would hide the temple-furnishing test aimed at a different audience. Rejected-route scope: Jer.27.16-Jer.27.22.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Does the exile letter close before the attached oracle concerning named prophets, or do sender, warnings, and judgments belong to one letter complex through 29:23?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.29.1-14 and Jer.29.15-23 with compulsory letter-complex hydration | retain Jer.29.1-23 as the only surfaced exile letter and attached warning
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.29.1-Jer.29.23. Controlling evidence: these-are-words-of-letter sender/recipient frame opens; build/plant/seek-peace exhortation, seventy-year promise and false-prophet warning close with Nebuchadnezzar judgment Scoped seam: Jer.29.1-Jer.29.23.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: split exhortation 29:4-14 from warnings or merge Shemaiah correspondence. Rejected-route scope: Jer.29.1-Jer.29.23.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should Rachel's lament, Ephraim's confession, and the return-road appeal surface as three children, or remain one consolation dialogue through the difficult 31:22 saying?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.31.15-17, Jer.31.18-20, and Jer.31.21-22 under a common consolation parent | retain Jer.31.15-22 as the only surfaced lament, comfort, and return appeal
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.31.15-Jer.31.22. Controlling evidence: Rachel's Ramah weeping receives hope, Ephraim's overheard self-correction receives compassion, and virgin Israel is told to mark the road home. Scoped seam: Jer.31.15-Jer.31.22.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Splitting Rachel and Ephraim would understate the shared child-return logic that culminates in road markers. Rejected-route scope: Jer.31.15-Jer.31.22.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Within the received WEB-MT coordinates, should branch and royal-priestly promise separate from the day-night covenant reply, while the shorter Greek form remains an unresolved witness question?

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: split 33:14-18 from 33:19-26 or import omission as preferred. Rejected-route scope: Jer.33.14-Jer.33.26.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the dated siege frame in 39:1-2 surface separately from breach, officials, royal capture, and population disposition in 39:3-10?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.39.1-2 and Jer.39.3-10 with fall-scene hydration | retain Jer.39.1-10 as the only surfaced Jerusalem-fall narrative
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.39.1-Jer.39.10. Controlling evidence: Siege dates culminate in a breach, Babylonian officials occupy the middle gate, Zedekiah flees and is captured and judged, while city destruction, deportation, and poor-land grants summarize the fall. Scoped seam: Jer.39.1-Jer.39.10.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: A seam after 39:7 would separate the king's fate from the city's parallel collapse and population disposition. Rejected-route scope: Jer.39.1-Jer.39.10.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the Ramah release remain independently retrievable from the 39:11-14 release notice, or should the overlapping scenes always be hydrated together without harmonizing them?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.40.1-6 with mandatory Jer.39.11-40.6 overlap hydration | retain Jer.40.1-6 as a child but never return it without the Jer.37-40 siege-and-release parent
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6. Controlling evidence: A new word heading locates Jeremiah bound among deportees at Ramah; the captain interprets the disaster, frees him, offers Babylon or Judah, and Jeremiah chooses Gedaliah at Mizpah. Scoped seam: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Collapsing this with 39:11-14 would suppress distinct location, captor speech, and choice details rather than resolve their relationship. Rejected-route scope: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the dated Baruch oracle remain only at its received position after chapter 44, or be cross-hydrated with the chapter 36 scroll scene without moving either text?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: retain Jer.45.1-5 at its received coordinate and attach a non-ordering relation to Jer.36 | require Jer.36 and Jer.45 shared retrieval while preserving both received positions
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5. Controlling evidence: A fourth-year scroll-writing setting quotes Baruch's added-sorrow complaint; the response announces universal uprooting, forbids seeking greatness, and grants life as spoil. Scoped seam: Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Joining the nations superscription at 46:1 would combine a private scribe oracle with a new collection title. Rejected-route scope: Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the fear-not saying surface as a separate epilogue, attach to the Egypt oracle, or be treated only as a received-order duplicate relation to 30:10-11?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: surface Jer.46.27-28 as a hydrated Egypt-collection epilogue with a non-authorizing duplicate relation | attach Jer.46.27-28 to Jer.46.13-26 under the complete Egypt oracle parent
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.46.27-Jer.46.28. Controlling evidence: A direct fear-not address to Jacob and Israel promises distant rescue, quiet return, divine presence, nation-ending judgment, and measured correction. Scoped seam: Jer.46.27-Jer.46.28.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Including this in the Egypt invasion poem would bury the audience reversal and remnant-preserving reassurance. Rejected-route scope: Jer.46.27-Jer.46.28.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should the Seraiah scroll sign surface as the received-order close of the Babylon collection while also hydrating its Zedekiah-journey frame, or be absorbed into a larger narrative relation?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: retain Jer.51.59-64 as a complete sign command-performance-interpretation child with nation-collection and journey hydration | surface it only within a larger Jer.46.1-51.64 Babylon-and-nations parent while preserving the dated narrative relation
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.51.59-Jer.51.64. Controlling evidence: A fourth-year journey setting commissions Seraiah with Jeremiah's written Babylon disasters; he must read, pray, bind the scroll to a stone, cast it into Euphrates, and interpret Babylon's sinking. Scoped seam: Jer.51.59-Jer.51.64.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Ending at 51:58 would omit the enacted scroll sign and the explicit end-of-Jeremiah-words subscription that closes the collection. Rejected-route scope: Jer.51.59-Jer.51.64.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Does the grave-desecration scene at 8:1-3 remain the final escalation of the Topheth burial judgment, or begin a new aftermath unit?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: Retain one cross-chapter Topheth-to-graves coda because at-that-time continues the same burial reversal and 8:3 supplies its survivor endpoint. | Open a separate 8:1-3 aftermath oracle because the temporal formula resets the scene from Topheth bodies to ancestral and royal graves.
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.7.29-Jer.8.3. Controlling evidence: Cut-hair lament, Topheth renaming, carrion exposure, silenced celebration, and royal-priestly grave desecration form one escalating defilement judgment across the chapter seam. Scoped seam: Jer.7.29-Jer.8.3.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: The 7:34/8:1 chapter division was rejected because at-that-time continues the same burial reversal; a separate 8:1 opening remains plausible. Rejected-route scope: Jer.7.29-Jer.8.3.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Should 9:1 close the balm-and-harvest lament across the chapter boundary, and how should unresolved speaker shifts affect retrieval?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: Keep 8:18-9:1 together because grief, Daughter Zion, failed healing, and desired tears sustain one lament arc. | End at 8:22 and treat 9:1 as a new speaker turn or opening intensification in the next lament.
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.8.18-Jer.9.1. Controlling evidence: Unrelieved grief, Daughter Zion's distant cry, failed harvest, balm questions, and the wish for a fountain of tears form one lament despite the chapter division. Scoped seam: Jer.8.18-Jer.9.1.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Ending at 8:22 was rejected because 9:1 intensifies the same weeping desire; the precise speaker remains deliberately unresolved. Rejected-route scope: Jer.8.18-Jer.9.1.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Is the full idol-versus-Creator polemic one retrieval unit, or should hymnic and Aramaic/witness-sensitive movements surface as hydrated children?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: Retain 10:1-16 whole because crafted-idol impotence and Creator kingship form a sustained contrast ending with the inheritance confession. | Expose children around 10:5/6 and 10:11/12 with mandatory siblings, recognizing form and language changes without preferring a text order.
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.10.1-Jer.10.16. Controlling evidence: A house-of-Israel summons contrasts crafted immobile idols with the living King and Creator, culminating in the Maker-of-all and inheritance confession. Scoped seam: Jer.10.1-Jer.10.16.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Proposed seams at 10:5/6 and 10:11/12 remain secondary to the polemic's idol-versus-Creator frame; Aramaic and witness-order questions are not decided here. Rejected-route scope: Jer.10.1-Jer.10.16.

Scoped seam: Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Separating 27:1 from 27:2 or cutting before 27:4 would detach date and performance from the envoy message, while the regnal-name tension must not be harmonized. Rejected-route scope: Jer.27.1-Jer.27.11.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: May the settlement-and-restoration instruction and named false-prophet judgment be independently retrieved, or must Jeremiah's first exilic letter remain whole-only?

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: split exhortation 29:4-14 from warnings or merge Shemaiah correspondence. Rejected-route scope: Jer.29.1-Jer.29.23.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: split 33:14-18 from 33:19-26 or import omission as preferred. Rejected-route scope: Jer.33.14-Jer.33.26.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: How should the two received Jeremiah-release scenes be retrieved without collapsing their different locations, agents, speeches, and choices?
issue_resolution_ledger.source_alternative: Keep 39:11-14 and 40:1-6 as distinct route units linked by mandatory dual hydration. | Create a single noncontiguous or composite release dossier for retrieval while preserving both received scenes verbatim.
issue_resolution_ledger.ruling: Selected route: Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14, Jer.39.15-Jer.39.18, Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6. Controlling evidence: Nebuchadnezzar commands Nebuzaradan to protect Jeremiah; named officials implement the order by removing him from the guard court and entrusting him to Gedaliah. Scoped seam: Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14. A retrospective guard-court word commissions a personal message: city judgment will occur, but Ebedmelech will escape because he trusted. Scoped seam: Jer.39.15-Jer.39.18. A new word heading locates Jeremiah bound among deportees at Ramah; the captain interprets the disaster, frees him, offers Babylon or Judah, and Jeremiah chooses Gedaliah at Mizpah. Scoped seam: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6.
issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Harmonizing this directly with 40:1-6 would erase the received text's second release setting; both scenes remain distinct but relationally hydrated. Rejected-route scope: Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14. Attaching this to his rescue action at 38:7-13 would violate the received placement and obscure its own word-event frame. Rejected-route scope: Jer.39.15-Jer.39.18. Collapsing this with 39:11-14 would suppress distinct location, captor speech, and choice details rather than resolve their relationship. Rejected-route scope: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Reject both a single undifferentiated Jer.1.4-19 retrieval object and naked retrieval of either vision without the call parent.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Reject a chapter seam at 3:25/4:1 as automatic authority and reject a single 3:6-4:4 child that obscures the voice shifts.

issue_resolution_ledger.source_question_or_challenge: Whole-chapter objects conceal poem, speaker, summons, and commission resets; small alarm or old-path fragments would invite devotional or political prooftexting.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Reject both the three whole-chapter chunks and verse-sized extraction at each trumpet, peace, path, or refining image.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Reject 7:34/8:1 chapter fallback and reject isolated retrieval of 7:22, 7:31, 7:34, 8:22, or 9:1.

issue_resolution_ledger.rejected_route: Reject splitting any stage of 13:1-11 and reject one undifferentiated 13:12-27 child.
